title: A structured event log records store lifecycle events with defined fields
description: The store emits structured events at four defined moments: opened (at successful open), migrated (once per migration run that applied at least one migration, carrying the version transition and the list of versions applied), backupCheckpoint (on each snapshot completion), and closed (on graceful shutdown). Every event carries an event name, an ISO-8601 timestamp, and the fields defined for that event class. Consumers subscribe via a single sink function injected at open time.
rationale: Silent stores are stores that surprise the operator. A structured event log makes 'when did the store come up, what version did it migrate through, when did the last snapshot land' answerable from the log stream without a database query. The four events are the minimum viable surface: opened proves boot, migrated proves schema state, backupCheckpoint proves the recovery story is live, closed proves a clean shutdown.
